newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan late-trade stocks down on Wall Street fall.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan late-trade stocks down on Wall Street fall.

text.p: Taiwan's share index punched briefly through 9,000 points but failed to sustain the momentum, falling slightly in late Tuesday trade as Wall Street's plunge inspired local profit-takers, brokers said.
U.S. stocks tumbled on Monday after Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto set off waves of profit-taking with comments about potential sale of U.S. government securities by Japan.
With 50 minutes left at 0310 GMT, Taiwan's index was down 28.34 points or 0.32 percent at 8,896.78.
Turnover was brisk at T$120 billion.
Analysts said the Wall Street fallout would be limited.

"Wall Street's fall should have little impact on Taiwan stocks. Investors simply are using this as an excuse to take profits after the index's recent surge," said HSBC James Capel research manager Alex Chen.

"It's the same situation in the U.S. In fact, since Japan mainly holds U.S. treasury bills, Hashimoto's comments should have little impact on U.S. stocks. But American investors used this an excuse to take profits on recent U.S. gains."
Taiwan construction shares were up 3.51 percent, but financials and electronics were lower.
